haiku-low.q1: Only the SHA-256 hash (token_hash) is stored. Plaintext appears only in the create response, shown once with a Copy button, and in the browser while the dialog is open.
haiku-low.q2: They cannot. The plaintext is shown exactly once and nobody can show it again, including support and engineering. The user must create a new token.
haiku-low.q3: The create request returns 409 with a message telling the user to revoke a token first. Nothing is inserted.
haiku-low.q4: On its next API request, because every request reads the row and token validity is never cached.
haiku-low.q5: A 401 with the same generic body in every case. The responses do not differ.
haiku-low.q6: The server SHA-256 hashes the presented token and finds the row by hash. The row must be not revoked and not expired to be usable.
haiku-low.q7: Any API request using the token triggers it. A single conditional update writes only when last_used_at is null or more than 1 hour old.
haiku-low.q8: The request still succeeds. The error is logged without the token.
haiku-low.q9: It sets revoked_at to now on the row. The list returns only active tokens, so the revoked token disappears from it.
haiku-low.q10: The update matches no row, so the response is 404, the same as for an unknown token. Revoking an already-revoked token is harmless and also returns 404.
haiku-low.q11: An active token row remains that counts toward the limit of 10, but nobody holds the plaintext. The user finds it by name in the list, revokes it, and creates a new one.

sonnet.q1: Only the SHA-256 hash is stored (token_hash in api_tokens). Plaintext appears only in the 201 create response, shown once in the create dialog (browser holds it only while the dialog is open). Never in DB, logs or analytics.
sonnet.q2: They can't. Plaintext is shown exactly once and nobody (including support/engineering) can show it again. They must create a new token.
sonnet.q3: The server returns 409 with the message 'Revoke a token first'; nothing is inserted.
sonnet.q4: On the very next API request; validity is never cached and every request reads the row.
sonnet.q5: 401 with the same generic body in every case (missing header, unknown, revoked, expired); the responses do not differ.
sonnet.q6: The server SHA-256 hashes the presented token and finds the row by token_hash. The row is usable only if it is not revoked (revoked_at null) and not expired.
sonnet.q7: A valid API request triggers a conditional update setting last_used_at = now only WHERE it is null or older than 1 hour. That condition limits it to about one write per token per hour.
sonnet.q8: The request still succeeds; the error is logged without the token.
sonnet.q9: Sets revoked_at = now on the row (filtered by id and user_id and not already revoked). The token is no longer active, so it no longer appears in the list (list shows active tokens only).
sonnet.q10: It returns 404 in both cases (another user's token looks the same as nonexistent; second revoke returns 404), and nothing is changed.
sonnet.q11: An active token row exists that nobody holds; it counts toward the limit of 10. The user finds it in the list by name, revokes it, then creates a new one. The server does not resend since it cannot recover the plaintext.
